# Microsoft Store submission (StoreBroker)

`publish-store.yml` submits the release's MSIX to the Microsoft Store using
Microsoft's [StoreBroker](https://github.com/microsoft/StoreBroker) PowerShell
module, via `Submit-ToMicrosoftStore.ps1` in this directory.

`microsoft/store-submission@v1` (the GitHub Action originally used here) turned
out to only implement win32 (EXE/MSI) submissions despite advertising a
`packaged` type — MSIX support was never built
([issue #12](https://github.com/microsoft/store-submission/issues/12), open
since Aug 2022). StoreBroker is Microsoft's own tool and actually supports
packaged-app submissions.

## `sbConfig.json`

The workflow calls `Update-ApplicationSubmission` with only `-ReplacePackages`
— it swaps in the new MSIX and nothing else. Because of that, only the
`packageParameters` block (consumed by `New-SubmissionPackage`) actually takes
effect. The `appSubmission` block is StoreBroker's standard scaffolding
(generated by `New-StoreBrokerConfigFile`) and is **not** applied to the live
listing unless the workflow starts passing the matching switch — e.g.
`-UpdateAppProperties` for `applicationCategory`, `-UpdatePricingAndAvailability`
for `pricing`, `-UpdatePublishModeAndVisibility` for `targetPublishMode`/
`visibility`. See StoreBroker's
[USAGE.md](https://github.com/microsoft/StoreBroker/blob/master/Documentation/USAGE.md#the-easy-way)
for the full switch list. If a future change adds one of those switches, update
this file first — it won't reflect the real listing until then.
